c6:gaziantep house.aciklama: This is a museum about the Whirling Dervishes. It's housed in a fine mansion, and shows displays. It is part of a mosque's "külliye" (Islamic-Ottoman social complex centered around a mosque). It was built in the 17th century. The Mevlevi Lodge Monastery is entered via a courtyard which opens off the courtyard of the mosque. Elsewhere I found it probably belonged to the Tekke Mosque, The mosque was built in 1638 by a Turkmen landowner, Mustafa Aga.

It was built in the 17th century. The Mevlevi Lodge Monastery is entered via a courtyard which opens off the courtyard of the mosque. Elsewhere I found it probably belonged to the Tekke Mosque, The mosque was built in 1638 by a Turkmen landowner, Mustafa Aga.

Termessos was a Pisidian city built at an altitude of more than 1000 meters at the south-west side of the mountain Solymos (modern day Güllük Dağı) in the Taurus Mountains (modern day Antalya province, Turkey). It lies 30 kilometres to the north-west of Antalya. It was founded on a natural platform on top of Güllük Dağı, soaring to a height of 1.665 metres from among the surrounding travertine mountains of Antalya, which average only 200 metres above sea level.

c6:lpg gas pump.aciklama: LPG Bullets The Bullets, named because of their shape stored Liquefied Petroleum Gases. LPG is the generic name for commercial Propane and commercial Butane. The two smaller vessels V1085 and V1086 stored Propane and were designated as emergency vaporisers for the Refinery Fuel Gas Main. V1092 and V1093 stored a combination of Butane and Propane which was pumped to process units to be separated. V1094 the furthest of the vessels was converted to be a buffer vessel for the Refinery Fuel Gas Main.

c6:red tower alanya historical tower.aciklama: The Kizil Kule (Red Tower) The octagonal shaped building that's the symbol of the city is a work by Selcuks of the 13th century. c6:kemer municipality.baslik: File:Višnjica Spring Dabrica settlement Bosnia and Herzegovina.jpg
c6:kemer municipality.aciklama: The photograph depicts a wide shot and the structural design of the Višnjica spring in Dabrica. In the foreground is a massive stone vault (volt), a traditional architectural element built from hewn stone to protect the spring from sunlight, contamination, and external elements. This type of covering allowed for the preservation of lower water temperatures and quality during summer months. Connected concrete troughs forming a functional unit for water distribution are also visible.

This increase is usually caused by technical problems on the road or in the means of transport, other times it is caused by the behavior of drivers on the road. The fight against road safety can be a priority concern of the State and this fight must be waged against the most vulnerable road user

c6:kemer pipe.aciklama: Pipe smoking lady. Dressed in late Ottoman urban style. She wears baggy trousers (‘şalvar’), a white cotton skirt (‘pamuklu gömlek’), a silk headscarf adorned with a lace border (‘oyalı yazma’), a gown (‘üçetek’, wich means: robe with three panels) and a belt with a big buckle (‘tokalı kemer’). The latter two are antique pieces: 19th century for the buckle, 1st half of the 20th century for the ücetek. On the floor: a big ‘cicim’ carpet (pronounced “jijim”). c6:manavgat manavgat coast.aciklama: Side is an ancient Greek city on the southern Mediterranean coast of Turkey, a resort town and one of the best-known classical sites in the country. It lies near Manavgat and the village of Selimiye, 78 km from Antalya in the province of Antalya. It is located on the eastern part of the Pamphylian coast, which lies about 20 km east of the mouth of the Eurymedon River. Today, as in antiquity, the ancient city is situated on a small north-south peninsula about 1 km long and 400 m across.

c6:antalya clouds.baslik: File:Antalya museum Uşak medallion carpet, 16th century carpet 4858.jpg
c6:antalya clouds.aciklama: Uşak medallion carpet, 16th century carpet. It is huge, six or seven meters wide, I'd guess. Uşak (110 km west of Afyon) was one of the most important and renowned carpet centers in Ottoman times (late 15th to 18th century). Rug production is still going on today, but on a lesser level and with altered designs. In the 17th century great quantities of Uşak carpets were made for the royal houses and the Christian churches of Europe. They are named according to their specific design: ‘star’, ‘medal
c6:antalya clouds.nesne: Antalya museum Uşak medallion carpet, 16th century carpet 4858

c6:london aviation fair.aciklama: The V-1 (Vergeltungswaffe Eins, or Vengeance Weapon One), was the world's first operational cruise missile. This name was given to it by the Nazi Propaganda Ministry, but the original Air Ministry designation was Fi 103, after its airframe designer, the Fieseler company. Powered by a simple but noisy pulsejet that earned it the Allied nicknames of "buzz bomb" and "doodle bug," more than 20,000 were launched at British and continental targets, mostly London and Antwerp, from June 1944 to March 19

c6:mediterranean coastal road.aciklama: The Copernicus Sentinel-2B satellite captured this true-colour image on 5 February 2019, just three days after heavy rainfall in Rome and the surrounding area of Lazio , Italy. It shows sediment gushing into the Tyrrhenian Sea , part of the Mediterranean Sea. The downpour on 2 February led to flooded streets, the closing of the banks of the Tiber River and several roads. The Tiber River can be seen snaking its way southwards in the image. The third longest river in Italy, it rises in the Apennin

c6:mediterranean coastal road.aciklama: Westward view across the buildings above Cala d'Estellencs on the northwestern coast of Mallorca. In the foreground are several traditional Mallorcan-style stone buildings, including the property currently rented as Cala Estellencs House . The Camí de la Mar, one of the two access roads leading down to the cove, passes between the buildings, which are surrounded by retaining walls, stairways and small terraces. Further uphill on the left, another stone house stands on a rocky coastal slope cover

c6:united kingdom flute.aciklama: Flute casts at Donkey Quarry near Broughton in Furness, Cumbria, England. These are excellent turbidite sequence flute casts. Possibly the best exposure in the UK. They are part of the Gawthwaite Formation (425 Ma, Silurian). These are shelf deposits which saw fast flows of sediment settle out into various grades. This is the bottom of a flow which scoured out the seabed (Iapetus) forming these features. They show the bed has been tilted by 90 degrees.

c6:united kingdom flute.aciklama: Flute Casts These knobbly shapes are indicative of turbidites, which are rocks formed by underwater slumps and landslides. The turbulent current carves hollows in the underlying rocks, and the hollows are then filled with sediment. This face is the underside of the flow; the rocks in this quarry have been tilted beyond the vertical. These turbidites are of Silurian age.

cf:File:Ex-Istanbul trolleybus in Izmir,.aciklama: An ex-Istanbul trolleybus in Izmir, turning around at Alsancak terminus (at Alsancak railway station). This batch of Izmir trolleybuses, acquired secondhand from the Istanbul trolleybus system after that system's closure in 1984, were Pistoiesi/Aerfer-bodied Alfa Romeo 910F vehicles built between 1961 and 1962. The fleet number visible on this one appears to be 131. The Izmir trolleybus system closed in 1992.

c6:atatürk street.aciklama: Atatürk Monument in Albany, Western Australia

This has nothing to do with Atatürk but with the house. This contraption enabled people, in particular women, to look into the street without being seen themselves. Many Turkish cities have an Atatürk Museum, often in a house where the founder of the Turkish Republic stayed at some time, sometimes for just one night. This is the Gaziantep version, for a stay on January 26, 1933, in a house from 1892.

This monument (named ‘Atatürk anıtı’ = Atatürk Memorial) dates from around 1930. Atatürk is portrayed as commander in chief of the Turkish armies. To the left stands a village woman in traditional Türkmen dress, carrying a bouquet of roses. To the right, a militia warrior holds the corner of a carpet; he wears the costume of the local ‘Zeybek’. Zeybeks (or Zeibeks), were irregular militia and guerrilla fighters living in the Aegean Region of the Ottoman Empire from late 17th to early 20th centur

c6:yesiloz.baslik: File:CAPPADOCIA Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites. World Heritage List. Turkey. Hot Air Ballooning Cappadocia.jpg
c6:yesiloz.aciklama: Hot Air Ballooning Cappadocia: A must do in Cappadocia is take a balloon ride in order to see the sights from a vantage point like no other. On this 1-hour flight at sunrise you will experience the changing colors and the unique landscapes that scatter the region. Enjoy a unique hot air balloon flight over the fairy chimneys and rock cut churches. This exhilarating experience in Cappadocia is one of the best places around the world to fly with hot air balloons. www.britannica.com/place/Cappadoci
c6:yesiloz.nesne: CAPPADOCIA Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites. World Heritage List. Turkey. Hot Air Ballooning Cappadocia

c6:yesiloz.aciklama: THE FAIRY CHIMNEYS In the days before tourism local people called the strange rock cones that surrounded them kales, or 'castles'. Nowadays these amazing structures are usually called peribacalari, or 'fairy chimneys'. They come in an extraordinary range of shapes and sizes but most are tall and phallic-shaped with a cap of harder stone that protects the softer rock underneath from erosion. c6:aksu ministry building.aciklama: It is an artificial lake built 13 kilometers south of Bolu city center. The surface of the lake, whose height is 1217 meters, is 4.5 hectares and its circumference is about 1300 meters. The view of the lake, which is covered with pine, fir, beech, hornbeam and mixed species of trees, is wonderful in every season. On the edge of the lake, which is covered with the extraordinary beauty of nature, there is a cute building, which is the "State Guesthouse" of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry.

c6:serenity queen.aciklama: Gunung Kawi Temple, also known as Gunung Kawi cliff temple, is an enchanting 11th-century temple and funerary complex nestled in the village of Tampaksiring, Bali. This protected archaeological site spans both banks of the Pakerisan River, captivating visitors with its unique location carved into the rock cliffside. Legend has it that Gunung Kawi Temple got its name from the combination of "Gunung" meaning "mountain" and "Kawi" referring to "sculpture," signifying a temple carved on a mountain.

The building fills a city block bounded by George, Market, York and Druitt Streets. The building fills a city block bounded by George, Market, York and Druitt Streets. c6:side ancient city.aciklama: Side is a city on the southern Mediterranean coast of Turkey. It includes the modern resort town and the ruins of the ancient city of Side, one of the best-known classical sites in the country. It lies near Manavgat and the village of Selimiye, 78 km from Antalya in the province of Antalya.[1]

c6:side museum.aciklama: The rulers of the Gupta dynasty unified northern India under native rule for the first time since the Maurya empire (323-185 bc). The Guptas named themselves after Chandragupta, the founder of the Maurya dynasty. This coin of Chandragupta II, who ruled from around ad 380 to 415, depicts a divine archer holding a bow and arrow. On the reverse is the Indian goddess of good fortune, Shri, seated on a lotus.

c6:side ancient city historical columns.aciklama: Column Street (or Column Avenue) of the ancient city of Side, Turkey (VII century BC). Marble columns are located along the edges of the avenue, the sidewalk is paved with mosaic tiles. The length of the street is about 250 m, width - 20 m. The street originates at the City Gates and leads to the ancient temples and houses of the rich citizens of the ancient city. The name Colonnade(d) Avenue can be found in some historical sources.

c6:antalya antalya city center.aciklama: Kaleiçi is the historic city center of Antalya, Turkey. Until modern times, almost the entire city was confined within its walls. It has structures dating from the Roman, Byzantine, Seljuk, Ottoman and modern Turkish republican eras. The Kaleiçi area is located in the centre-eastern portion of the city along the mediterranean coast fronted by the yacht harbour that dates to the Roman era. The name Kaleiçi means "Inside the Kale" or "Inner Kale" (Kale itself means castle or fortress).

c6:antalya antalya city center.aciklama: Kurshunlu Waterfall Nature Park is located in Aksu district of Antalya province, Turkey, 6-7 km to the east of the city center. The park is famous for a waterfall and a variety of plants and animals. It is one of favourite recreational spots for locals and a famous destination for tourists. On the photo the part of the Kurshunlu waterfall, a pond and surrounding plant variety are shown. The photo was captured in June, 2018.

c6:antalya antalya city center.aciklama: Ruins of Pinara, ancient Lycian city in Asia Minor, close to Fethiye, Antalya Province, Turkey. September, 2025. Pinara, PinalePilleñni The city of Pinara is located on the eastern slopes of the South Antikragos Mountains (Baba Dağı) to the east of Fethiye Bay and overlooks the Xanthos Valley. It was built on terraces rising from 330 meters to 715 meters. It is bordered by the cities of Xanthos in the south and Tlos in the northeast. The Lycian name of the city was Pinale (or Pilleñni). c6:aqua fit.aciklama: There will be no clean water highlights the extreme effects of climate change in Eswatini. Droughts have ravaged the country now and again in the past resulting in shortages of water supply and pollution has worsened the situation at hand. Climate change has also caused frequent heatwaves. This remains an eye opener and a strong motivator to society that employing certain efforts towards mitigating the present and future effects of climate change can be proved to be very important.
